title: Elon Musk's Flying Car: Real Tech or PR Stunt? (Learn Native English)

subtitles.en:
Hello everyone! Welcome back to the AB
English Podcast... Well, I'm Mia!
subtitles.zh:
大家好！歡迎回到 AB
English Podcast... 我是 Mia！

subtitles.en:
And I'm Alex! Wow, it's just so exciting to
have you with us today!
subtitles.zh:
我是 Alex！哇，今天能有大家
一起參與真的太棒了！

subtitles.en:
Alex, did you see that video—the one that
completely broke the internet yesterday?!
subtitles.zh:
Alex，你有看到那段影片嗎——就是昨天
在網路上引爆轟動的那支？！

subtitles.en:
Oh, you mean the Tesla event down in Texas?
You know... the one where Elon Musk showed
off an actual "flying car"?
subtitles.zh:
噢，妳是指在德州舉辦的特斯拉發表會嗎？
就是... 馬斯克炫耀展示那台
真正「飛行車」的活動？

subtitles.en:
Yes! The new Tesla Roadster! I mean... it
literally used rocket thrusters to blast into
the air!
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！新款的 Tesla Roadster！我說... 它
真的用了火箭推進器直接衝上空中耶！

subtitles.en:
Haha, yeah, I saw that! It literally jumped
off a ramp... hovered for a few seconds, and
then landed smoothly!
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，對，我有看到！它真的從斜坡上飛躍...
懸浮了幾秒鐘，然後平穩地降落！

subtitles.en:
Well, over in Taiwan, netizens are already
cracking jokes: "Finally! A car that can just
fly straight over the Snow Mountain Tunnel
traffic!"
subtitles.zh:
在台灣，網友們早就已經在開玩笑了：
「終於！有一台車可以直接飛過雪山隧道的
塞車車潮了！」

subtitles.en:
Haha, wow, that would be amazing, wouldn't
it? But—well, people around the world are
locked in a really heated debate right now.
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，哇，那真的會超棒的，不是嗎？
但——全球的網友現在正陷入
極為熱烈的爭論呢。

subtitles.en: Hmm, a debate? Wait—between who exactly?
subtitles.zh: 嗯，爭論？等等——到底具體是誰跟誰在吵？

subtitles.en:
Well... between folks who believe this is the
breakthrough future of transportation—and
those who insist it's completely ridiculous!
subtitles.zh:
嗯... 就是深信這是未來交通重大突破的人，
與堅持這根本荒謬至極的人
這兩派之間的論戰！

subtitles.en:
Oh, that makes total sense! I mean, whenever
Elon Musk makes any announcement... people
just lose their minds!
subtitles.zh:
噢，這完全合情合理！我是說，只要馬斯克
一公布任何消息... 大家就會集體陷入狂熱！

subtitles.en:
Exactly! And you know, as English learners...
viral news stories like this are absolute
gold!
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！而且妳知道嗎，對英語學習者來說...
像這種爆紅的發燒新聞簡直是絕佳寶藏！

subtitles.en: Oh? Why do you say that, Alex?
subtitles.zh: 噢？Alex，你為什麼會這麼說呢？

subtitles.en:
Well, because native speakers use very
specific idioms and vocabulary when
discussing hype... skepticism... and crazy
futuristic tech!
subtitles.zh:
因為母語人士在討論話題炒作、懷疑態度...
以及狂野的未來黑科技時，
會使用非常特定的慣用語與單字！

subtitles.en:
Oh, I love that! So... today, we're going to
learn how to talk about breaking news and
futuristic tech—just like a pro?
subtitles.zh:
噢，我很喜歡這個切入點！所以... 今天我們要學
如何像個專業人士一樣，暢聊即時頭條與未來科技？

subtitles.en:
You bet! Today, we're breaking down five
essential expressions you can drop into
conversation... whenever you hear wild news!
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！今天我們要解析五個核心表達方式，
每當你聽到瘋狂的新聞時...
就能直接在對話中派上用場！

subtitles.en:
Awesome! So, Alex... what did Elon Musk
actually promise about this car anyway?
subtitles.zh:
太棒了！那 Alex... 馬斯克到底對這台車
誇下了什麼海口？

subtitles.en:
Well, he claimed this supercar was co-
developed with SpaceX—using actual cold-gas
thrusters!
subtitles.zh:
嗯，他聲稱這款超跑是與 SpaceX 共同開發的——
配備了真正的冷氣推進器！

subtitles.en:
Wow... cold-gas thrusters?! That sounds
straight out of a sci-fi blockbuster!
subtitles.zh:
哇... 冷氣推進器？！聽起來根本是
科幻賣座大片裡才有的東西吧！

subtitles.en:
Haha, it really does! And—get this—he stated
that production would start in 2028... with a
price tag over two hundred and fifty thousand
dollars!
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，真的超像！而且——妳聽好了——他宣稱
會在 2028 年開始量產... 售價超過
二十五萬美元！

subtitles.en:
Hmm... production in 2028? Well, knowing his
track record with promised deadlines... can
we really believe that?
subtitles.zh:
嗯... 2028 年量產？以他過去對承諾交付日期的
跳票紀錄來看... 我們真的能信嗎？

subtitles.en:
Ah! Bingo! That brings us right to our very
first essential idiom today!
subtitles.zh:
啊！答對了！這正好帶出我們今天
要介紹的第一個必學片語！

subtitles.en:
When someone makes a massive claim that
sounds too good to be true... you should
always: "Take it with a grain of salt."
subtitles.zh:
當有人誇大其詞、宣稱的事情聽起來好到不真實時...
你應該永遠："Take it with a grain of salt."

subtitles.en:
Hmm, "Take it with a grain of salt"? Like...
literally adding a grain of salt to your
food?
subtitles.zh:
嗯，"Take it with a grain of salt"？字面意思是...
在食物裡加一粒鹽？

subtitles.en:
Haha, exactly! But figuratively—it means to
approach something with skepticism... not
believing it completely.
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，沒錯！但比喻上的意思是——帶著懷疑
去看待某件事... 不要完全相信。

subtitles.en:
Wow, where on earth does such a strange
expression even come from?
subtitles.zh: 哇，這麼奇怪的說法到底是從哪裡演變來的？

subtitles.en:
Well, it actually traces back to ancient
Rome! See... an ancient recipe for a poison
antidote claimed it would only work—if
swallowed with a tiny grain of salt!
subtitles.zh:
其實可以追溯到古羅馬時期！據說... 有一份古老的
解毒劑配方宣稱，只有配著一小粒鹽吞下去——
解藥才會發揮療效！

subtitles.en:
Oh, I get it! So the salt made the bitter
antidote a little easier to swallow!
subtitles.zh:
噢，我懂了！所以鹽是為了讓苦澀的解藥
稍微容易吞下去一點！

subtitles.en:
Exactly! So, if Elon Musk promises flying
cars by 2028, you can say: "I love his
ambition, but—well—I take his timeline with a
grain of salt."
subtitles.zh:
完全正確！所以如果馬斯克承諾 2028 年推出飛行車，
你可以說："I love his ambition, but—well—I take
his timeline with a grain of salt."

subtitles.en:
Ah! "I take it with a grain of salt." Wow,
that's incredibly useful! But wait—can I use
it when a coworker shares juicy office
gossip?
subtitles.zh:
啊！"I take it with a grain of salt." 哇，
這句超級好用！等等——那如果同事跟我分享
辦公室八卦，我也可以用這句嗎？

subtitles.en:
Oh, one hundred percent! Like: "Hey, don't
believe everything Sarah says... take it with
a grain of salt!"
subtitles.zh:
噢，百分之百可以！比如："Hey, don't believe
everything Sarah says... take it with a grain of salt!"

subtitles.en:
Got it! But, Alex... let's look closer at the
car itself. Was it really "flying"—or was it
honestly just jumping?
subtitles.zh:
學起來了！不過 Alex... 我們仔細看那輛車本身，
它真的是在「飛行」——還是說穿了只是在跳躍？

subtitles.en:
Well, that's the billion-dollar question!
Experts point out it didn't fly
continuously—it simply used quick bursts of
compressed cold air to leap off the ground!
subtitles.zh:
嗯，這就是價值數十億美元的大哉問了！
專家指出它並不是持續飛行——只是利用壓縮冷空氣
短暫瞬間爆發，讓車子跳離地面而已！

subtitles.en:
Hmm... so it's not a genuine flying vehicle,
like an electric vertical takeoff aircraft?
subtitles.zh:
嗯... 所以它並不是真正的飛行載具，
不像電動垂直起降飛行器那樣？

subtitles.en:
Not at all! And—well, that's precisely why
many critics are labeling the whole spectacle
a... "publicity stunt."
subtitles.zh:
完全不是！而且——這正是為什麼許多評論家
把整場壯觀表演貼上... "publicity stunt" 的標籤。

subtitles.en:
Hmm... a "publicity stunt"? What does that
actually mean?
subtitles.zh: 嗯... "publicity stunt"？這到底是什麼意思？

subtitles.en:
Well, "publicity" refers to media buzz and
attention—while a "stunt" is an extravagant,
daring action.
subtitles.zh:
嗯，"publicity" 指的是媒體輿論關注度——
而 "stunt" 則是大膽、浮誇的噱頭動作。

subtitles.en:
Oh, I see! So a "publicity stunt" is
basically an orchestrated move designed just
to grab headlines... and get free media
attention!
subtitles.zh:
噢，我懂了！所以 "publicity stunt"（公關噱頭）
基本上就是精心策劃的舉動，純粹是為了登上新聞頭條...
博取免費的媒體曝光！

subtitles.en:
Spot on! Companies frequently stage wild
stunts just to pump their stock price—or
build massive viral hype.
subtitles.zh:
一點也沒錯！許多企業經常搞出瘋狂噱頭，
就只是為了拉抬股價——或是製造病毒式的狂熱話題。

subtitles.en:
Haha, and Elon Musk is hands-down the
undisputed king of publicity stunts!
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，那馬斯克絕對是無可爭議的
公關炒作之王了！

subtitles.en:
Oh, totally! I mean... remember when he
launched his own red Tesla into outer space?
subtitles.zh:
噢，完全是！我是說... 還記得他把自己的
紅色特斯拉跑車發射到外太空去的時候嗎？

subtitles.en:
Wow, how could anyone possibly forget that?!
That was—hands down—the ultimate publicity
stunt in human history!
subtitles.zh:
哇，怎麼可能有人會忘記那個？！
那絕對是——無庸置疑——人類歷史上
最極致的公關噱頭！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. So, well... is this new Roadster
just a flashy gimmick, or is it—you
know—something much bigger?
subtitles.zh:
沒錯。所以說... 這款新 Roadster 究竟只是個華而不實的
花招，還是——有更深遠的意義？

subtitles.en:
Hmm, let's dive deeper into the technology
behind it!
subtitles.zh: 嗯，讓我們更深入探討它背後的工程技術吧！

subtitles.en:
Well, credit where credit is due—from an
engineering standpoint... what they did is
just incredible.
subtitles.zh:
平心而論——單從工程的角度來看...
他們做到的事情確實很不可思議。

subtitles.en:
How so? I mean... what makes cold-gas
thrusters so special on an actual car?
subtitles.zh:
怎麼說？我是說... 在一輛真正的車上裝
冷氣推進器到底有什麼特別的？

subtitles.en:
Usually, sports cars rely on downforce to
stay glued to the road. But Tesla... they're
using rocket thrusters to literally—defy
gravity!
subtitles.zh:
一般跑車都是依靠下壓力牢牢貼緊路面。
但特斯拉... 他們卻是用火箭推進器
真正做到了——defy gravity（對抗地心引力）！

subtitles.en:
'Defy gravity'! Oh, wait... I know that from
the musical 'Wicked'! There's that famous
song, 'Defying Gravity'!
subtitles.zh:
'Defy gravity'！噢等等... 我在音樂劇《女巫前傳》
聽過這個！裡面有一首名曲就叫 'Defying Gravity'！

subtitles.en:
Yes, exactly! 'Defy' basically means to
resist or refuse to obey. So... 'defy
gravity' literally means to float or fly—just
ignoring gravitational pull entirely.
subtitles.zh:
沒錯，正是那樣！'Defy' 基本上就是反抗或拒絕服從的意思。
所以... 'defy gravity' 字面上就是懸浮或飛行——
完全無視重力的束縛。

subtitles.en:
Hmm, and what about figuratively? Can we use
it in everyday conversation?
subtitles.zh:
嗯，那比喻層面呢？我們在日常對話中
也可以使用它嗎？

subtitles.en:
Absolutely! When something achieves
impossible success against all odds... well,
you can say it 'defies gravity.'
subtitles.zh:
當然可以！當某件事打破一切常理、逆勢取得
看似不可能的成就時... 你就可以說它 'defies gravity'。

subtitles.en:
Oh! Like... 'Despite the economic crisis,
that tech company's stock price continues to
defy gravity!'
subtitles.zh:
噢！就像... 'Despite the economic crisis, that tech
company's stock price continues to defy gravity!'
（儘管面臨經濟危機，那家科技公司的股價依然逆勢狂飆！）

subtitles.en:
Wow, Mia, that's a brilliant example! You
totally nailed it!
subtitles.zh: 哇，Mia，這個例句舉得太棒了！完全切中要點！

subtitles.en:
Well, thank you! And if this car actually
hits the market... would you consider it a
'game changer'?
subtitles.zh:
謝謝！那如果這台車真的正式上市發售...
你會認為它是個 'game changer' 嗎？

subtitles.en:
Oh, without question! A 'game changer'—well,
that's definitely our next must-know phrase.
subtitles.zh:
噢，毫無疑問！'Game changer'——這絕對是
我們下一個必須掌握的短語。

subtitles.en:
Right, so a 'game changer' refers to an
event, idea, or innovation that completely
transforms the way things are done... right?
subtitles.zh:
沒錯，所以 'game changer' 是指徹底改變事物
既定運作方式的重大事件、理念或創新... 對吧？

subtitles.en:
Exactly. The original iPhone was a total game
changer for mobile phones, and Netflix...
well, Netflix was a game changer for home
entertainment.
subtitles.zh:
沒錯。當年的初代 iPhone 徹底顛覆了手機產業，
而 Netflix... 嗯，Netflix 則是顛覆了整個家庭娛樂市場。

subtitles.en:
Hmm... so if cars start leaping over
obstacles or firing rocket boosters, that
could truly be a game changer for the entire
auto industry!
subtitles.zh:
嗯... 所以如果汽車開始能躍過障礙物或噴射火箭推進，
那對整個汽車產業來說，真的會是個 game changer！

subtitles.en:
Yes... but there's a huge catch, Mia—and it
has nothing to do with engineering.
subtitles.zh:
是的... 但 Mia，這裡有個巨大的隱憂——
而且這與工程技術毫無關係。

subtitles.en:
Wait, nothing to do with engineering? Then...
what is it?
subtitles.zh: 等等，跟工程無關？那... 究竟是什麼？

subtitles.en:
Well, it's about safety, the law—and the
government!
subtitles.zh: 嗯，這關乎公共安全、法規——以及政府審查！

subtitles.en:
Oh, right! Just imagine... waiting at a red
light, and the car behind you accidentally
fires its rocket thrusters right into your
bumper!
subtitles.zh:
噢，對耶！想像一下... 你在等紅燈時，
後面那台車不小心啟動了火箭推進器，
直接朝你的後保險桿噴射過來！

subtitles.en:
Haha, exactly! Or imagine pedestrians on the
sidewalk... just getting blown right off
their feet!
subtitles.zh:
哈哈，沒錯！或者想像人行道上的行人...
直接被強大的推進氣流吹飛翻滾！

subtitles.en:
Wow... that sounds like an absolute nightmare
for city planners!
subtitles.zh: 哇... 這對都市規劃人員來說簡直是一場惡夢！

subtitles.en:
Which brings us directly to our next big
concepts—'regulatory hurdles' and the classic
'Catch-22'!
subtitles.zh:
這正好引出我們接下來的重大概念——
'regulatory hurdles'（法規障礙）以及經典的 'Catch-22'！

subtitles.en:
Oh, tell me more! How on earth do government
regulators even begin to handle a rocket car?
subtitles.zh:
噢，快多告訴我一些！政府監管部門到底該如何
著手去規範一輛會飛的火箭車？

subtitles.en:
Well, in the business world, whenever you
deal with government agencies—like aviation
or highway safety boards—you face serious
'regulatory hurdles.'
subtitles.zh:
在商業世界中，只要你跟政府機關打交道——
比如民航局或公路交通安全管理局——
你就會面臨嚴峻的 'regulatory hurdles'。

subtitles.en:
Ah, 'regulatory hurdles'—obstacles created by
official laws and regulations!
subtitles.zh:
啊，'regulatory hurdles'——也就是官方法律與法規
所設立的重重阻礙！

subtitles.en:
Right! And that puts Tesla in a classic...
'Catch-22.'
subtitles.zh:
沒錯！而這讓特斯拉陷入了經典的...
'Catch-22'。

subtitles.en:
'Catch-22'? Hmm, I've heard that phrase so
many times, but what does it actually mean?
subtitles.zh:
'Catch-22'？嗯，我聽過這詞很多次，
但它真正的含意到底是什麼？

subtitles.en:
Well, a 'Catch-22' is a frustrating dilemma—a
trap from which you cannot escape simply
because of contradictory rules.
subtitles.zh:
'Catch-22' 是一種令人無奈的兩難困境——
一個因為互為矛盾的規則而讓你永遠無法逃脫的陷阱。

subtitles.en:
Wait... where does the number 22 even come
from?
subtitles.zh: 等等... 這個 22 的數字到底打哪來的？

subtitles.en:
It comes from a famous 1961 novel by Joseph
Heller. In the story, World War Two pilots
could only be excused from dangerous combat
missions... if they were officially declared
insane.
subtitles.zh:
它源自約瑟夫·海勒（Joseph Heller）在 1961 年寫的著名小說。
在故事中，二戰飛行員只有在被正式診斷為精神失常時...
才能免於執行危險的作戰任務。

subtitles.en:
Okay... so could they just claim to be crazy,
then?
subtitles.zh: 好啊... 那他們直接聲稱自己瘋了不就好了？

subtitles.en:
But here's the catch! Wanting to be excused
actually proved you were completely
sane—because you cared about your own life!
So... you still had to fly!
subtitles.zh:
但矛盾陷阱就在這裡！申請免飛這件事，
反而證明了你精神完全正常——因為你在乎自己的生命！
所以... 你還是必須去出任務！

subtitles.en:
Wow, that is delightfully evil! It's a
completely inescapable paradox!
subtitles.zh:
哇，這設定真是有夠絕妙又折磨人！
根本是個完全無法破解的悖論嘛！

subtitles.en:
Exactly! And for a flying car... well,
regulators won't approve it until it's proven
safe in public conditions, but—you can't test
it in public without their approval!
subtitles.zh:
完全正確！而套用在飛行車上... 監管單位在確認其在
公共環境絕對安全前不會核准；但——沒有他們的批准，
你根本不能在公共環境中測試！

subtitles.en:
Wow, talk about the ultimate Catch-22! No
wonder people think it might take way longer
than 2028...
subtitles.zh:
哇，這真的是最典型的 Catch-22！難怪大家都覺得
這件事耗費的時間可能會遠遠超過 2028 年...

subtitles.en:
Well, alright Mia! Let's put our listeners to
the test with a quick practice challenge!
subtitles.zh:
好啦 Mia！讓我們用一個快速的情境小測驗
來考驗一下聽眾吧！

subtitles.en:
Oh, I'm ready! Hit me with your best
scenario, Alex!
subtitles.zh: 噢，我準備好了！Alex，儘管出招吧！

subtitles.en:
Well, imagine this... your coworker leans
over and says: 'Hey, our company is giving
everyone a 50% raise next month!' Hmm, what
idiom should you say to them?
subtitles.zh:
想像一下... 你的同事靠過來神秘兮兮地說：
「嘿，我們公司下個月要給所有人加薪 50% 耶！」
嗯，這時候你應該對他們回覆哪句片語？

subtitles.en:
Oh, that's way too easy! I'd definitely say:
'Well, I'd take that rumor with a huge grain
of salt!'
subtitles.zh:
噢，這也太簡單了吧！我肯定會說：
"Well, I'd take that rumor with a huge grain of salt!"
（我對這個傳言抱持極大懷疑／聽聽就好啦！）

subtitles.en:
Perfect! 100 points! You used it like a true
native speaker!
subtitles.zh:
太完美了！給你 100 分！妳用得跟
道地的英語母語人士一模一樣！

subtitles.en:
If you're listening right now, let us know
your thoughts on flying cars in the comments
below!
subtitles.zh:
如果你現在正在收聽，歡迎在下方留言區
分享你對飛行車的看法！

subtitles.en:
Remember, listening is great, but speaking is
where real fluency happens.
subtitles.zh:
請記住，聽力輸入固然很棒，但唯有開口說
才能真正建立英語流利度。

subtitles.en:
Check our video description for our two free
GugoPro language learning tools!
subtitles.zh:
歡迎查看影片資訊欄，探索我們提供的兩款
免費 GugoPro 語言學習工具！

subtitles.en:
Practice listening with the L-Player, and
speak one-on-one with the AI Speaking Tutor.
subtitles.zh:
使用 L-Player 練習精準聽力，並透過 AI 口說家教
進行一對一語音對話練習。

subtitles.en:
Thank you so much for joining us today. Keep
practicing, and we'll see you in the next
episode!
subtitles.zh:
非常感謝大家今天的收聽。持續保持練習，
我們下一期節目見囉！
